title: Worst-Case Optimal $\sqrt{\epsilon}$-Rate Stability of KL Divergence under Perturbations of Gaussian Distributions
abstract: arXiv:2604.11026v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We establish a stability bound for the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence when its Gaussian reference distribution is perturbed. Existing relaxed triangle inequalities of KL divergence between Gaussian distributions require all three distributions to be Gaussian, which limits their use in applications such as out-of-distribution detection with flow-based generative models. Let $\mathcal{N}_1$ and $\mathcal{N}_2$ be $d$-dimensional Gaussian distributions, and let $P$ be any $d$-dimensional distribution satisfying $\mathbb{E}_P[\|X\|^2]<\infty$ and $\mathrm{KL}(P\Vert \mathcal{N}_1)<\infty$. If $\mathrm{KL}(\mathcal{N}_1\Vert\mathcal{N}_2)\leq\epsilon$ for $0<\epsilon<1/12$, we give an upper bound of $\left|\mathrm{KL}(P\Vert\mathcal{N}_1)-\mathrm{KL}(P\Vert\mathcal{N}_2)\right|$. Under suitable uniform boundedness conditions, the bound is $ \frac{\sqrt{6d\epsilon}}{2}+K\sqrt{\epsilon}+o(\sqrt{\epsilon})$ as $\epsilon\rightarrow 0$

translated_title: 高斯分布扰动下KL散度的最坏情形最优 $\sqrt{\epsilon}$ 阶稳定性
translated_abstract: 我们为库尔贝克-莱布勒（KL）散度在其高斯参考分布受到扰动时建立了一个稳定性界。现有的高斯分布之间KL散度的松弛三角不等式要求三个分布全部为高斯分布，这限制了它们在诸如基于流的生成模型的分布外检测等应用中的使用。设 $\mathcal{N}_1$ 和 $\mathcal{N}_2$ 为 $d$ 维高斯分布，$P$ 为任意满足 $\mathbb{E}_P[\|X\|^2]<\infty$ 且 $\mathrm{KL}(P\Vert \mathcal{N}_1)<\infty$ 的 $d$ 维分布。若当 $0<\epsilon<1/12$ 时有 $\mathrm{KL}(\mathcal{N}_1\Vert\mathcal{N}_2)\leq\epsilon$，我们给出了 $\left|\mathrm{KL}(P\Vert\mathcal{N}_1)-\mathrm{KL}(P\Vert\mathcal{N}_2)\right|$ 的上界。在适当的均匀有界条件下，当 $\epsilon\rightarrow 0$ 时，该界为 $\frac{\sqrt{6d\epsilon}}{2}+K\sqrt{\epsilon}+o(\sqrt{\epsilon})$。
tldr: 本文在比较分布 $P$ 不必为高斯分布的情况下，首次建立了高斯参考分布受扰动时KL散度变化的最坏情形最优 $\sqrt{\epsilon}$ 阶稳定性界，突破了现有松弛三角不等式要求三个分布均为高斯分布的局限，可应用于流生成模型的分布外检测等场景。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes a worst-case optimal $\sqrt{\epsilon}$-rate stability bound for KL divergence under perturbations of the Gaussian reference distribution—without requiring the third distribution to be Gaussian—thereby overcoming the limitations of existing relaxed triangle inequalities and enabling applications such as out-of-distribution detection with flow-based generative models.
